events.title: IBM ThinkPad 700C released
events.summary: [IBM] launched the ThinkPad 700C in October 1992 — a laptop with a 10.4-inch color display, TrackPoint, and a folding keyboard design.
events.about: The ThinkPad became the default corporate laptop — developers carried them between meetings, [VPN]'d into Unix servers, and ran early Windows IDEs. The TrackPoint and durable magnesium shell set expectations for business portables. Lenovo later acquired the line, but the 700C defined what a serious laptop looked like.

narrative.whyChosen: The ThinkPad 700C established the design language and build quality of business laptops.
narrative.whyImportant: It made portable computing standard for enterprise developers and road warriors.
narrative.problemSolved: Business travelers needed a rugged, full-featured laptop that could replace a desktop on the road.
